newsitem.title: USA: New York State Bruno not optimistic about budget.
newsitem.headline: New York State Bruno not optimistic about budget.

text.p: The New York State Senate Majority Leader was not optimistic that the state would get a new budget anytime soon, pinning the blame squarely on his Democratic opponents in the Assembly.

"The budget that we were supposed to have adopted on April 1 may not get adopted in the next couple of months primarily because, in my estimation there is not a will on the part of the Assembly to do a budget, and you can't help but talk about the lack of a budget without out getting somewhat partisan," said Joseph Bruno, R-Troy.
The state last year failed to reach a budget until 104 days past the April 1 deadline, and this spring again started a new fiscal year without a pact.
Bruno spoke at a luncheon sponsored by the New York Building Congress, an association for design and construction professionals.

The Senate Majority Leader, who is battling with the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, over the Senate's plan to end apartment rent regulations, noted there were lots of other issues that had to be thrashed out before a budget could be reached. Bruno listed welfare and criminal justice reforms, building maximum security prisons, and energy deregulation.
He told reporters that budget talks between Gov George Pataki, a Republican, Silver and himself, as well as between their staffs, would continue during a two-week legislative spring break.
